full_text_en:
**Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, Gao Juan v. Shanghai Xianglong Yuji Construction Development Co., Ltd. and Huang Zhengbing — dispute over liability for injury to a service provider**

**Ruling Summary**

Pursuant to Article 48 of the Construction Law of the PRC, it is a statutory obligation for construction enterprises to participate in work-related injury insurance and pay premiums for their employees, whereas arranging accident insurance and paying premiums for employees engaged in hazardous operations is an encouraged requirement. Where a construction enterprise has arranged accident insurance for employees engaged in hazardous work, this does not exempt the enterprise from its statutory obligation to pay work-related injury insurance premiums for its employees. Pursuant to Article 39 of the Insurance Law of the PRC, where an policyholder insures the personal accident insurance for workers with whom it has a labor relationship, it may not designate any person other than the insured or his/her close relatives as the beneficiary. Where a construction enterprise, as the policyholder, purchases group accident insurance for workers, the beneficiaries of such insurance can only be the workers or their close relatives. If a worker suffers personal injury or death in the course of work and the construction enterprise or the actual constructor claims to deduct the accident insurance proceeds from the compensation amount, thereby effectively becoming the beneficiary of such insurance in a disguised form, such claim violates the legislative purpose and shall not be supported according to law.

**Plaintiff: Fan Zhongxing**, male, born January 13, 1933, Han ethnicity, residing in Qidong City, Jiangsu Province.

**Plaintiff: Yu Lanping**, female, born February 18, 1954, Han ethnicity, residing in Qidong City, Jiangsu Province.

**Plaintiff: Gao Juan**, female, born October 14, 1981, Han ethnicity, residing in Nantong City, Jiangsu Province.

**Defendant: Shanghai Xianglong Yuji Construction Development Co., Ltd.**, domiciled at No. xxx, Tianyaoqiao South Road, Shanghai.

Legal representative: Xie Lianming, Executive Director of the company.

**Defendant: Huang Zhengbing**, male, born January 13, 1964, Han ethnicity, residing in Qidong City, Jiangsu Province.

The plaintiffs, Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan, instituted an action in the Qidong City People's Court of Jiangsu Province against the defendants, Shanghai Xianglong Yuji Construction Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xianglong Company) and Huang Zhengbing, concerning a dispute over liability for injury to a service provider.

**Plaintiffs' Allegations**
The plaintiffs Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan alleged: In February 2018, after the defendant Xianglong Company contracted the construction of the office building and workshop of Jiangsu Wodi Biotechnology Co., Ltd. located on Haizhou Road in the Qidong High-tech Industrial Development Zone, it subcontracted the project to the defendant Huang Zhengbing. Fan Hongchang (the deceased) was employed by Huang Zhengbing as a carpenter. At approximately 4:00 p.m. on October 3, 2018, while Fan Hongchang was working on the construction site, a square timber fell and struck him on the head, shattering his safety helmet and causing a head injury. The two defendants failed to promptly send him to a medical facility for examination and treatment after he was injured. At noon on October 6, 2018, as his dizziness worsened, Fan Hongchang, accompanied by his wife, rode an electric bicycle to seek medical treatment. During this journey, he fell. He was rushed to Qidong People's Hospital in a state of deep coma and, despite rescue efforts, died the following day. On October 9, 2018, the Qidong Municipal Public Security Bureau commissioned Suzhou Tongji Judicial Appraisal Institute to conduct a forensic examination of the cause of Fan Hongchang's death. On December 18, 2018, the institute issued an appraisal opinion concluding that Fan Hongchang's death was caused by severe craniocerebral trauma and chest trauma, with the craniocerebral trauma being the primary cause of death and the chest trauma being a secondary cause. The plaintiffs argued that an employment relationship existed between Fan Hongchang and Huang Zhengbing. Since the employee died from a safety accident while performing employment activities, the employer should bear compensation liability. Xianglong Company, knowing that Huang Zhengbing lacked the appropriate qualifications, subcontracted the project and should bear joint and several liability according to law. To protect their legitimate rights and interests, the plaintiffs sued the court pursuant to legal provisions, requesting a judgment: 1. Ordering Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing to jointly compensate Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan for various losses, including medical expenses, death compensation, funeral expenses, dependent's living expenses, and body storage fees (up to June 3, 2019), totaling RMB 1,065,987.73; 2. Ordering Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing to pay body storage fees at the rate of RMB 100 per day from June 4, 2019, until the judgment takes effect; 3. Ordering Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing to bear the litigation costs.

**Defendants' Defense**
The defendants Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing argued: The appraisal institution conducted the appraisal blindly without ascertaining what the falling object was, which not only contravenes the relevant provisions on judicial appraisal but also affects the analysis and determination of Fan Hongchang's cause of death. In the two to three days after being struck on the head by a falling object at the construction site, Fan Hongchang reported to work normally and showed no signs of discomfort. The judicial appraisal did not clearly distinguish or determine the respective contributions of the two separate injuries to Fan Hongchang's death, which violates the procedural requirements for judicial appraisal. Therefore, the appraisal opinion issued by Suzhou Tongji Judicial Appraisal Institute cannot serve as a basis for the plaintiffs' claim for compensation against the defendants. The court is requested to conduct a new appraisal of Fan Hongchang's cause of death and the apportionment of responsibility for the two injuries. Based on the available evidence, the cause of Fan Hongchang's death could only be a single-vehicle traffic accident. On the morning of the single-vehicle accident, Fan Hongchang was still working at the construction site. He was known to enjoy drinking alcohol, and the scene of the single-vehicle accident indicated he was riding at high speed. In any event, even if Fan Hongchang's death had a causal relationship with the injury from the falling object at the construction site, that would be a secondary cause. The primary cause should be the multiple injuries sustained from the single-vehicle accident.

**Facts Found by the Qidong People's Court at First Instance**

From February to October 2018, Fan Hongchang was employed by the defendant Huang Zhengbing at a daily wage of RMB 180. On the afternoon of October 3, 2018, while working on the construction project of the office building and workshop of Jiangsu Wodi Biotechnology Co., Ltd. located on Haizhou Road in the Qidong High-tech Industrial Development Zone, Fan Hongchang was struck on the head by a falling square timber. On October 6, 2018, Fan Hongchang was involved in a single-vehicle traffic accident while riding an electric bicycle. He died the following day despite rescue efforts. On October 9, 2018, the Accident Investigation Division of the Qidong Municipal Public Security Bureau Traffic Police Brigade commissioned Suzhou Tongji Judicial Appraisal Institute to conduct a forensic medical examination to determine the cause of Fan Hongchang's death. The appraisal opinion issued by the institute on December 18, 2018, stated: Fan Hongchang's cause of death was severe craniocerebral trauma and chest trauma, with craniocerebral trauma being the primary cause of death and chest trauma being a secondary cause. Regarding the manner of injury and the role of the two separate traumas in causing Fan Hongchang's death, a fall could not cause skull cracking or mild deformation, nor could it fully explain all the chest injuries. That is, the head injury and the right chest and back injury were likely caused by the first impact (the falling object). However, based on the pre-existing head and chest injuries, the subsequent fall causing force to the face and chest could certainly exacerbate those pre-existing head and chest injuries. This likely constitutes the pathological basis for Fan Hongchang's deep coma and weak spontaneous breathing after the single-vehicle accident.

Separately, it was found that the defendant Xianglong Company had purchased group accident insurance for Fan Hongchang from China Life Insurance Co., Ltd. After the incident, the plaintiffs Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan received insurance proceeds of RMB 100,000.

It was further found that the defendant Xianglong Company undertook the construction of the office building and workshop project of Jiangsu Wodi Biotechnology Co., Ltd. on Haizhou Road in the Qidong High-tech Industrial Development Zone and provided scaffolding, square timbers, and other materials for the project. The defendant Huang Zhengbing undertook the carpentry labor services from Xianglong Company. Huang Zhengbing lacked the corresponding construction qualifications. Fan Hongchang's father, Fan Zhongxing, was born on January 13, 1933. Fan Zhongxing also had two daughters, Gao Caiping and Gao Caiqin.

**Opinion of the Qidong People's Court at First Instance**

The right to life and health of citizens is protected by law. According to law, where a labor relationship is formed between individuals, if a service provider is injured in the course of providing services, liability shall be borne according to the respective fault of both parties. The issue in dispute in this case concerns the fault of each party in the incident. Pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Tort Law of the PRC, when the deceased Fan Hongchang was injured in the course of providing services, liability should be apportioned between the recipient of the services and the service provider based on their respective fault. In this case, Fan Hongchang was struck on the head by a falling square timber while working, causing head injuries and right chest and back injuries. The subsequent fall in the single-vehicle accident exacerbated the pre-existing injuries, leading to death. The appraisal opinion also indicated that craniocerebral trauma was the primary cause of death and chest trauma a secondary cause. Therefore, Fan Hongchang himself bore fault for the occurrence of this incident. The defendant Huang Zhengbing, as the recipient of services, should also bear corresponding compensation liability for the injuries sustained by Fan Hongchang in the course of providing services. The defendant Xianglong Company subcontracted the carpentry labor services to Huang Zhengbing, who lacked the corresponding construction qualifications, failed to properly manage the site, and failed to provide a safe working environment. Therefore, Xianglong Company also bore fault for the occurrence of this incident and should bear corresponding compensation liability. Taking into account the degree of fault of each party, the court of first instance determined that Huang Zhengbing should bear 50% of the losses, Xianglong Company should bear 20%, and the remaining losses should be borne by Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan themselves. Suzhou Tongji Judicial Appraisal Institute is an institution with the appropriate appraisal qualifications, and the appraisal opinion it issued can serve as a basis for Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan to claim the relevant losses. The appraisal opinion has already explained and clarified the role of the two incidents in causing Fan Hongchang's death. Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing did not submit any evidence to prove that the circumstances for recommencing the appraisal existed. Therefore, the application of Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing for a new appraisal was not granted.

Regarding the determination of losses. The plaintiffs Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan claimed medical expenses of RMB 16,443.70, which are confirmed by corresponding medical expense receipts and medication details. The court of first instance confirmed this amount. The plaintiffs' claims for hospitalization meal subsidies of RMB 36 (RMB 18/day × 2 days), nursing fees of RMB 396 (2 days × RMB 99/day × 2 persons), lost wages of RMB 360 (RMB 180/day × 2 days), and dependent's living expenses of RMB 46,210 (RMB 27,726 × 5 years ÷ 3 persons) are legally grounded and were approved by the court of first instance. The plaintiffs' claim for funeral expenses of RMB 36,342 complies with legal provisions and was supported. Regarding the plaintiffs' claim for body storage fees, as such expenses fall within the scope of funeral expenses, claiming such fees in addition to the already supported funeral expenses constitutes a duplicate claim. Therefore, the plaintiffs' claim for body storage fees was not supported. The plaintiffs' claim for death compensation of RMB 896,800 (RMB 47,200/year × 19 years) was supported because Fan Hongchang's main source of livelihood before his death was non-agricultural income, and the plaintiffs' calculation using the urban standard has a corresponding factual and legal basis. The plaintiffs' claim for transportation, accommodation, and lost wages incurred by the family members of the victim in handling the incident and funeral arrangements was determined at RMB 3,000. The total losses of Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan amounted to RMB 999,587.70. After deducting the insurance proceeds of RMB 100,000 received from the group accident insurance purchased by Xianglong Company for Fan Hongchang, the actual losses of Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan were RMB 899,587.70. Huang Zhengbing shall bear 50% of this amount, i.e., RMB 449,793.85; Xianglong Company shall bear 20%, i.e., RMB 179,917.54; the remaining losses shall be borne by Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan themselves. Regarding the plaintiffs' claim for moral damages, as Fan Hongchang's death caused considerable mental distress to Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan, considering the degree of fault of both parties, and with a view to manifesting the justice of the law and fostering good customs, moral damages were determined at RMB 30,000, of which Huang Zhengbing shall pay RMB 20,000 and Xianglong Company shall pay RMB 10,000.

Accordingly, the Qidong People's Court, pursuant to Articles 16, 22, 26, and 35 of the Tort Law of the PRC, and Articles 10, 17, and 18 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Compensation for Personal Injury, rendered the following judgment on June 27, 2019:

1. The defendant Huang Zhengbing shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes legal effect, compensate the plaintiffs Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan for various losses totaling RMB 469,793.85;
2. The defendant Xianglong Company shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes legal effect, compensate the plaintiffs Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan for various losses totaling RMB 189,917.54;
3. The other claims of the plaintiffs Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan are dismissed.

Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Nantong Intermediate People's Court, arguing:

1. Pursuant to Article 11, paragraph 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Compensation for Personal Injury, Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing should bear joint and several compensation liability.
2. Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing should bear full compensation liability for all losses of the appellants, and Fan Hongchang bore no fault in this incident.
3. The RMB 100,000 in group accident insurance proceeds received by the appellants should not be deducted. According to Article 46 of the Insurance Law of the PRC, after suffering personal injury, the insured may receive compensation of two different natures.
4. The body storage fees additionally paid by the appellants due to the litigation exceed the scope of funeral expenses as defined by law and should be borne by Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing.

In summary, the appellants argued that the first instance judgment erred in its factual findings and requested the court of second instance to set aside the first instance judgment and render a new judgment in accordance with the law.

**The appellees Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing argued in defense:**

1. Pursuant to Article 35 of the Tort Law of the PRC, the first instance court correctly determined that Xianglong Company bore 20% liability.
2. In this case, Fan Hongchang was indeed injured by the square timber at the construction site, but the cause of his death also included the traffic accident. Therefore, the first instance court's determination that Fan Hongchang bore 30% liability has a factual basis.
3. The RMB 100,000 group accident insurance was purchased by the employer Huang Zhengbing for Fan Hongchang, and the premiums were also paid by Huang Zhengbing. Therefore, the beneficiary of this insurance should be Huang Zhengbing.
4. Body storage fees fall within the scope of funeral expenses, and funeral expenses have already been calculated in this case.

In summary, the appellees argued that the first instance court correctly found the facts and applied the law, and the judgment should be upheld.

The Nantong Intermediate People's Court, upon hearing the appeal, confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

During the second instance, the appellants Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan submitted two sets of evidence: the group accident insurance policy from China Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Nantong Branch, and invoices for body storage and transportation fees, to prove: (1) The policyholder was Xianglong Company, not Huang Zhengbing, and the insured was Fan Hongchang; (2) The body storage and transportation fees should be borne by Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing. Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing, in their cross-examination, acknowledged the authenticity of the insurance policy information but argued that since the accident insurance premiums were borne by Xianglong Company, Xianglong Company should be the beneficiary. They argued that body storage and transportation fees fall within the scope of funeral expenses and should not be calculated separately. Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing also submitted to the court insurance policies for work-related injury insurance and accident insurance purchased for other employees, as well as a set of witness statements, to prove that Xianglong Company had no statutory obligation to purchase accident insurance, and that the costs of accident insurance and work-related injury insurance for employees were all borne by Xianglong Company and not deducted from employee wages. Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan, in their cross-examination, acknowledged the authenticity of the work-related injury and accident insurance policies but argued they were irrelevant to this case. They did not confirm the authenticity or relevance of the other evidence.

The court found that the authenticity of the accident insurance policy for Fan Hongchang and the invoices for body storage and transportation fees was confirmed. The witness statements provided by Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing were only written statements, and their authenticity was not confirmed. The relevance of the other evidence was not confirmed.

**Opinion of the Nantong Intermediate People's Court at Second Instance**

The issues in dispute in this appeal are: (1) Whether the appellee Xianglong Company and the appellee Huang Zhengbing should bear joint and several compensation liability; (2) Whether the RMB 100,000 in accident insurance proceeds involved in this case should be deducted from the compensation amounts payable by Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing; (3) Whether the determination of the liability percentages in this case is correct; (4) Whether body storage fees and transportation fees fall within the scope of funeral expenses.

**Regarding Issue One**, the appellee Xianglong Company should bear joint and several compensation liability with the appellee Huang Zhengbing.

Pursuant to Article 11, paragraph 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Compensation for Personal Injury, where an employee suffers personal injury due to a safety accident in the course of performing employment activities, if the contractor or subcontractor knew or should have known that the employer who accepted the contract or subcontract lacked the corresponding qualifications or safety conditions, the contractor or subcontractor shall bear joint and several compensation liability with the employer. In this case, the appellee Xianglong Company subcontracted the project to the appellee Huang Zhengbing, who lacked construction qualifications. The victim Fan Hongchang was injured and subsequently died in the course of construction. For this personal injury, Xianglong Company should bear joint and several compensation liability with the actual constructor Huang Zhengbing.

**Regarding Issue Two**, the appellees Xianglong Company and Huang Zhengbing are not entitled to claim a deduction of the RMB 100,000 accident insurance proceeds from the compensation amount.

First, Article 48 of the Construction Law of the PRC provides that construction enterprises shall, in accordance with the law, participate in work-related injury insurance and pay work-related injury insurance premiums for their employees. Enterprises are encouraged to arrange accident insurance for employees engaged in hazardous operations and pay the premiums. That is, paying work-related injury insurance for employees is a statutory obligation of construction enterprises, while arranging accident insurance for employees engaged in hazardous work is an encouraged provision and is not mandatory. The purpose of the law in encouraging construction enterprises to arrange accident insurance for employees engaged in hazardous work is to provide additional protection for employees. However, it does not exempt construction enterprises from their statutory obligation to pay work-related injury insurance for employees. If a construction enterprise could use insurance proceeds received from arranging accident insurance for employees to offset its compensation liability to the employees, this would effectively allow the construction enterprise to avoid its statutory obligation to pay work-related injury insurance by arranging accident insurance, which clearly contradicts the legislative intent of that provision.

Secondly, from the perspective of the nature of accident insurance. Group accident insurance is not employer liability insurance. The beneficiary of such personal insurance is generally the insured or a person designated by the insured. Article 39 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates that the beneficiary of personal insurance shall be designated by the insured or the policy holder. When the policy holder designates the beneficiary, the consent of the insured is required. Where a policy holder purchases personal insurance for a worker with whom it has a labor relationship, it shall not designate any person other than the insured or the insured's close relatives as the beneficiary. The legislative intent of this provision is that employers and workers are often in an unequal position. When an employer purchases accident insurance for a worker, it may use its dominant position to designate itself as the beneficiary, which would inevitably harm the legitimate rights and interests of the worker in a disadvantaged position. Therefore, this provision explicitly states that when an employer purchases personal insurance for a worker, the beneficiary can only be the insured or the insured's close relatives. If a construction unit or employer, after purchasing accident insurance for its employees, could directly deduct the insurance proceeds from the compensation, the construction unit or employer would become a de facto beneficiary, which contravenes the legislative purpose of this provision. In this case, the Appellee, Xianglong Company, as the policy holder, purchased group accident insurance for Fan Hongchang. The beneficiary of this personal insurance was Fan Hongchang. After Fan Hongchang's death, his heirs are entitled to inherit the accident insurance proceeds. Even if Xianglong Company's subjective intent in purchasing accident insurance for Fan Hongchang was to mitigate its own liability for compensation, accident insurance is a type of personal insurance, not liability or property insurance. If Xianglong Company or the Appellee Huang Zhengbing wished to reduce employment risks, they should have lawfully contributed to work-related injury insurance for Fan Hongchang or purchased employer liability insurance, rather than substituting the obligation to purchase mandatory insurance by obtaining group personal accident insurance.

Thirdly, the insured under accident insurance is entitled to double recovery. Article 46 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where an insured suffers death, disability, illness, or other insured events due to the conduct of a third party, the insurer, having paid the insurance proceeds to the insured or the beneficiary, does not have the right of recourse against the third party. However, the insured or the beneficiary still has the right to claim compensation from the third party. According to this provision, because the insured's life or health has been damaged, and the loss cannot be measured or compensated in monetary terms, the insured or beneficiary may obtain double recovery, and the principle of indemnity applicable to property insurance does not apply in this context. In this case, Fan Hongchang was injured and subsequently died while providing labor for the Appellee Huang Zhengbing. His heirs are entitled to claim insurance proceeds from the insurance company under the accident insurance policy and also have the right to claim employer liability compensation from Fan Hongchang's employer, Huang Zhengbing. However, after paying the insurance proceeds, the insurer does not have the right of recourse against the employer Huang Zhengbing. In other words, both the personal accident insurance proceeds and the damages for death due to personal injury belong to the heirs of Fan Hongchang. The policy holder, Xianglong Company, does not have any interest in these amounts, and the employer, Huang Zhengbing, has even less right to demand a deduction of RMB 100,000 for accident insurance proceeds from the compensation amount.

Regarding Disputed Issue Three: In this case, the judicial expert opinion states: "In summary, Fan Hongchang's cause of death was severe craniocerebral trauma and chest trauma. The craniocerebral trauma was the primary cause of death, while the chest trauma was a secondary cause. The head injury and the right chest and back injury are considered to have been caused by the first impact. However, on the basis of the existing head and chest injuries, the force applied to the face and chest from the fall could certainly exacerbate the aforementioned head and chest injuries." After being injured while providing labor, Fan Hongchang did not immediately go to the hospital for examination but continued working the next day. He eventually died after being sent to the hospital due to a fall from his bicycle, and no medical treatment could save him. His delay in seeking treatment and his fall from the bicycle contributed to a certain extent to his death. The court of first instance accordingly found that Fan Hongchang should bear 30% of the liability, which was appropriate.

Regarding Disputed Issue Four: Funeral expenses are a standardized compensation item, meaning the specific amount spent on funeral arrangements is not considered; instead, the compensation amount is determined based on the uniform local standard. Expenses for the storage and transportation of the body are both costs incurred in the process of handling the funeral. Furthermore, in this case, the victim Fan Hongchang died on October 7, 2018. The appraisal process was initiated on October 9 of the same year. After the autopsy on October 26, the Suzhou Tongji Judicial Appraisal Institute issued the "Expert Opinion" on December 18 of that year. The deceased's family did not handle the remains until October 4, 2019. This part of the expenses represents losses that were expanded. Even if they exceed the standardized compensation amount for funeral expenses, they should be borne by the deceased's family.

Based on the foregoing, the total losses incurred by the Appellants Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan due to Fan Hongchang's death amounted to RMB 999,587.70. The Appellee Huang Zhengbing shall bear 70% of the compensation liability, i.e., RMB 699,711.39, plus RMB 30,000 for solatium (moral damages), totaling RMB 729,711.39. The Appellee Xianglong Company shall bear joint and several liability for compensation for this portion of the losses.

In conclusion, the appeal of the Appellants Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan is partially sustained, and this part is supported. The Nantong Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with paragraph 1, item 2 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on January 6, 2020:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (2018) Su 0681 Min Chu No. 9482 of the Qidong City People's Court of Jiangsu Province;

2. Huang Zhengbing shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes legal effect, compensate Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan for their various losses totaling RMB 729,711.39;

3. Shanghai Xianglong Yuji Construction Development Co., Ltd. shall bear joint and several liability for Huang Zhengbing's aforesaid compensation obligation;

4. Dismiss the other claims of Fan Zhongxing, Yu Lanping, and Gao Juan.

This judgment is final.
